stories.headline: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Trump Presses Board
stories.dek: Huang resigned Nov. 12 and returned Nov. 23, and lawmakers in both parties are demanding answers on national security.
pole_a_bullets: Huang is the central figure in keeping the U.S. ahead of China in AI chips, and Trump's defenders say removing him hands rivals an advantage.
The board voted unanimously after meetings it said left it satisfied on his candor, and Huang has not been charged with any crime.
His exit hit Nvidia's shares and unsettled the wider AI sector, so a stable CEO matters to the companies and investors building on its chips.
The new Chief Compliance Officer post and the continuing investigations are presented as safeguards, so reinstatement does not end accountability.
pole_b_bullets: A reported affair with a woman alleged to have Chinese intelligence ties is a counterintelligence matter that a brief internal review cannot settle, say Republican Sens. Cornyn and Ricketts and Rep. Bacon.
Nvidia cited input from senior U.S. officials, and Sen. Warren wants Congress told which officials gave it and what they said.
Critics say presidential pressure on a private board sets a troubling precedent, especially after the board chair said days earlier that Huang would not return.
Ricketts says the board still has to answer for unaccounted-for chips, and Warren and Schumer want export-control bills passed and investigations opened when Democrats take control in January.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions voiced by Trump and administration allies, and by investors who urged the board to keep Huang's return open.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions voiced by Republican and Democratic lawmakers including Cornyn, Ricketts, Bacon, Warren and Schumer.
evidence_left: Nvidia's Nov. 23 SEC filing says the board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, CEO and director. It also says Nvidia will cooperate with government investigations and search for a Chief Compliance Officer.
Huang resigned Nov. 12 after reports of extramarital affairs, one with a woman alleged to work with Chinese intelligence (The Hill). Nvidia's independent probe is ongoing.
evidence_right: Nvidia said it acted after input from senior levels of the U.S. government. Trump said he spoke with board members directly and indirectly (NBC News, CNBC).
Nvidia shares rose more than 30% on Nov. 23 (CNN). The Nasdaq Composite rose 6.51% and the S&P 500 rose 4.73%.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from NVIDIA Form 8-K (SEC), NBC News, Axios, CNBC, November 24, 2026.

stories.headline: Stocks Post Best Day Since April 2025 as Fed Hike Looms
stories.dek: A rebound after a steep sell-off collides with expectations of a December rate increase.
pole_a_bullets: The rally was broad. Every S&P 500 sector except energy and consumer staples rose, and 26 of 30 Dow stocks gained.
The fear gauge fell sharply, and the sell-off looks like a washout after seven straight down days.
Even after cutting its target, Yardeni's 7,500 year-end S&P 500 forecast implies a gain of more than 8.5% from current levels.
Commentators describe the economy as resilient, which supports earnings even with higher rates.
pole_b_bullets: One headline, Huang's return, drove much of the jump, and a single-company bounce is a thin basis for a durable recovery.
The Nasdaq remains 12.7% below its Oct. 6 peak, and the Dow is 8.75% below its Aug. 5 peak.
Fed officials expect a December hike, and markets are pricing out 2027 cuts. Higher borrowing costs weigh on valuations.
The VIX is still near 27 and futures slipped Tuesday, which suggests the bounce is fragile.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions commonly voiced by equity strategists and dip-buyers, such as Yardeni Research.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions commonly voiced by rate strategists and cautious analysts reading the same data.
evidence_left: On Nov. 23 the S&P 500 rose 4.73% to 7,237.17, the Nasdaq Composite rose 6.51%, and the Dow rose 1,447.98 points (3.01%) to 49,595.31 (CNN).
The prior week all three major indexes lost 8% or more. The S&P 500 fell seven straight days, its longest streak since February 2020 (CNN).
evidence_right: Fed minutes show nearly all officials expect a quarter-point hike in December. Two floated a half-point move, and CME FedWatch put the odds of a December hike near 95% (ABC News/AP).
Tuesday premarket, Nasdaq 100 futures were down 0.96% and S&P 500 futures down 0.38% (Benzinga).
stories.sources_line: Sourced from CNN, NBC News, ABC News/AP, Benzinga, November 24, 2026.

stories.headline: Trump Order Tells Contractors to Coordinate With White House on Congressional Probes
stories.dek: The order comes weeks before Democrats take the House and promise investigations.
pole_a_bullets: Executive privilege is a recognized presidential power, and the order protects privileged communications held by contractors.
Contractors that deal with the executive branch should not be exposed to partisan fishing expeditions, as the White House fact sheet argues.
Coordination is not refusal. Counsel Will Scharf said that whether subpoenas are honored depends on the subpoena.
Democrats have signaled sweeping probes, and the White House is entitled to prepare for them.
pole_b_bullets: Oversight is a core constitutional power of Congress, and Rep. Robert Garcia calls the order a blatant attack on it.
Letting the White House screen what contractors hand over invites concealment, and Garcia asks what the White House is trying to hide.
Democrats say the aim is to blunt investigations of alleged corruption, including matters involving Trump's family.
Rep. Jamie Raskin says the order has the force of an interoffice memo and that courts will back Congress.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions voiced by the White House counsel's office and administration allies.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions voiced by incoming House Democrats including Garcia and Raskin.
evidence_left: Trump's order directs federal contractors and subcontractors to consult the administration on congressional inquiries and withhold communications the White House deems privileged (NBC News).
Scharf told federal agencies they must get approval from his office and the Office of Legislative Affairs before appearing before Congress (NBC News).
evidence_right: Scharf told Democrats in writing that their probes may cross into criminality. He told Bloomberg the White House might not honor subpoenas, saying it depends on the subpoena (reported by Raw Story citing Bloomberg).
Scharf also told Democrats that document-retention requests from ranking members carry no weight (Punchbowl News).
stories.sources_line: Sourced from NBC News, Punchbowl News, Raw Story, November 24, 2026.

stories.headline: Trump Uses DOJ Speech to Attack Newsom Over 548 Death Row Commutations
stories.dek: Trump also announced a directive to seek more federal death sentences and to speed federal executions.
pole_a_bullets: Juries imposed these sentences, and a governor's mass commutation overrides their verdicts.
Victims' families say Newsom erased their closure without notice, and Trump put several of them on stage.
California voters just rejected a ballot measure to abolish the death penalty, and critics say Newsom acted against that result.
The new federal directive targets child murderers and rapists or traffickers who kill, and supporters call that a justified use of capital punishment.
pole_b_bullets: Newsom says state-sanctioned killing conflicts with California's values and that an imperfect legal system cannot be trusted to execute people.
Anti-death-penalty advocates say Trump is using the issue for political purposes that do not help victims' families.
Newsom accuses the administration of using the Justice Department against opponents while pardoning allies.
Commutation to life without parole keeps these prisoners locked up, and critics say the speech is aimed at a likely 2028 rival.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions voiced by Trump, Attorney General Todd Blanche and victims' family members.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions voiced by Newsom and anti-death-penalty advocates such as Natasha Minsker.
evidence_left: Newsom commuted the death sentences of 548 California inmates to life without parole (CNN, The Hill). The cases all stem from state prosecutions (Yahoo News).
Trump said at the Justice Department on Nov. 23 that the DOJ is working to overturn the commutations (The Hill).
evidence_right: Trump announced a directive for the DOJ to seek the death penalty for child murderers and for rapists and traffickers who kill, and to expedite federal executions (Yahoo News, The Hill).
A California ballot measure to abolish the death penalty was defeated by just over 6 points earlier this month (The Hill). Newsom imposed a moratorium in 2019.
stories.sources_line: Sourced from CNN, The Hill, MS NOW, November 24, 2026.

stories.headline: Governors Ask Congress for National AI Rules That Leave State Laws Standing
stories.dek: The bipartisan NGA principles collide with the White House push to preempt state AI laws.
pole_a_bullets: A patchwork of state rules raises compliance costs for companies operating across state lines, and the White House cites interstate commerce and national security.
Federal standards for the most advanced models would give developers one set of rules to follow.
A House discussion draft would preempt state laws for three years and bar state limits on model development, while leaving state rules on AI use (reported by Townhall citing Nextgov).
Utah Gov. Spencer Cox says states do not have to choose between innovation and safety, and the governors' plan says rules should not favor large firms.
pole_b_bullets: States are already acting, and New York's RAISE Act takes effect in January. Gov. Hochul is signing a five-year ban on AI-chatbot toys.
Governors want Washington to handle national risks, with states keeping authority over how AI is used on workers, consumers and children.
The NGA asks for independent audits of frontier models and reporting of serious safety incidents, and says any preemption should be approached cautiously.
No bill text yet combines the governors' split with the White House's preemption language, so broad preemption would leave a gap.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions voiced by the White House, congressional preemption backers and industry-aligned commentators.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions voiced by the bipartisan governors' council led by Wes Moore and Mike Braun, and by state AI-safety advocates.
evidence_left: The NGA released six AI principles on Nov. 22, from a council led by Maryland Gov. Wes Moore (D) and Indiana Gov. Mike Braun (R) (MLQ.ai, Townhall).
The White House asked Congress to override state AI laws that impose undue burdens (Intelligence Report). Its March 2026 framework recommended preempting certain state laws (NGA).
evidence_right: The governors urged Congress to approach preemption cautiously and to consult a cross-section of states (PYMNTS).
New York is set to be the second state, after California, to ban AI-chatbot toys, effective in February (NBC News).
stories.sources_line: Sourced from PYMNTS, Startup Fortune, NBC News, Intelligence Report, November 24, 2026.

stories.headline: Trump Pauses Army's Iowa Lead Azide Blast; Appeals Court Clears It
stories.dek: The planned detonation of about 9,500 pounds of degraded explosive is set for Nov. 25 amid dispute over the lead plume.
pole_a_bullets: The Army says a controlled detonation is the only way to dispose of the degraded material, and that doing nothing risks something worse.
Trump wrote that the material could explode on its own and that detonating now is safer.
The EPA approved an emergency permit, and the Eighth Circuit declined to block the operation.
Mitigation measures are being put in place, and the date was chosen for optimal weather conditions.
pole_b_bullets: Army modeling shows lead particles traveling up to 40 miles and dust drifting up to 100 miles, and lead is a known neurotoxin.
State officials, residents and the American Lung Association say communication was late and inadequate, and that eastern Iowa and western Illinois could be exposed.
Earthjustice sued for the Iowa Environmental Council and the Sierra Club's Iowa chapter to halt the detonation.
Trump's pause and conditions, including the incoming governor's sign-off, add confusion, and it is unclear whether he will keep insisting on them.
stories.pole_a_who: Positions voiced by the Army, the Trump administration and the Middletown mayor.
stories.pole_b_who: Positions voiced by Earthjustice, Iowa environmental groups, public-health groups and state officials seeking transparency.
evidence_left: The Army found the degraded lead azide in a March safety review and says controlled detonation is the only disposal option (PBS NewsHour). The EPA approved an emergency permit earlier this month (Yahoo News).
An appeals court on Nov. 23 declined to block the detonation, hours after Trump's pause (NBC News, CBS News).
evidence_right: Trump said on Nov. 23 that the Army should not proceed without approval from the Eighth Circuit and Gov.-elect Rob Sand (D) (Axios, CBS News).
The Army scheduled the detonation of 68 barrels, about 9,500 pounds, for Nov. 25 (Iowa Public Radio, PBS NewsHour).
stories.sources_line: Sourced from PBS NewsHour, Axios, CBS News, NBC News, November 24, 2026.
